name: id
description: Assigns a unique identifier to an element, used to target it from CSS, JavaScript or an in-page anchor link.
notes: Must be unique within the page — duplicate ids break getElementById and CSS specificity assumptions.

name: class
description: Assigns one or more space-separated class names to an element for styling with CSS or selection with JavaScript.
notes: Unlike id, class is not unique — many elements can share the same class.

name: style
description: Applies inline CSS declarations directly to a single element.
notes: Inline styles have very high specificity and are hard to override — prefer classes for anything reused.

name: src
description: Specifies the URL of an external resource to embed, used on elements like ,

name: href
description: Specifies the destination URL for a hyperlink or linked resource, used on <a> and <link>.
notes: A href starting with # links to an element with a matching id on the same page.

name: alt
description: Provides alternative text for an image, read by screen readers and shown if the image fails to load.
notes: Use alt="" (empty) for purely decorative images so screen readers skip them.

name: title
description: Provides advisory, supplementary text for an element, typically shown as a tooltip on hover.
notes: Not reliably accessible (not announced on focus by all screen readers) — don't rely on it as the sole source of critical information.

name: data-*
description: Custom attribute prefix for embedding private, page-specific data directly on an element, readable via JavaScript.
notes: Accessible in JS via the element's `dataset` property, which converts kebab-case to camelCase.

name: disabled
description: Disables a form control or button, greying it out and preventing user interaction and form submission of its value.
notes: A boolean attribute — its mere presence disables the element, regardless of its value.

name: placeholder
description: Shows hint text inside an empty <input> or <textarea> that disappears once the user starts typing.
notes: Not a substitute for a <label> — placeholder text disappears on input and isn't reliably accessible.

name: target
description: Specifies where to open a linked document or embedded frame — a new tab, the same frame, or a named frame.
example: Open in new tab
notes: Pair target="_blank" with rel="noopener" to prevent the new page from controlling the opener window.

name: rel
description: Describes the relationship between the current document and a linked resource, used on <a> and <link>.
parameters: Common values: noopener, noreferrer, nofollow, stylesheet, icon, preload.

name: tabindex
description: Controls whether an element is keyboard-focusable and its position in tab order.
parameters: 0 — focusable in natural DOM order. -1 — focusable only via script. Positive number — explicit (and discouraged) tab order.
notes: Avoid positive tabindex values — they create a confusing, hard-to-maintain tab order.

name: contenteditable
description: Makes an element's content directly editable by the user in the browser, like a rich-text field.
notes: Powers many rich-text editors, but requires care to sanitize user-generated HTML.

name: hidden
description: Hides an element from rendering entirely, equivalent to display: none, without removing it from the DOM.
notes: A boolean attribute; toggle it via JavaScript (el.hidden = true) to show/hide content.

name: draggable
description: Marks whether an element can be dragged using the native HTML Drag and Drop API.
notes: Most elements aren't draggable by default; images and links are exceptions.

name: lang
description: Declares the natural language of an element's content, helping screen readers use correct pronunciation and browsers offer translation.
notes: Should always be set on <html> at minimum.

name: dir
description: Sets the text direction of an element's content — left-to-right or right-to-left — for languages like Arabic or Hebrew.

name: spellcheck
description: Controls whether the browser checks the spelling and grammar of editable text content.
notes: Useful to disable on fields like usernames, codes or emails where spellcheck underlines are noise.

name: download
description: Tells the browser to download the linked resource as a file instead of navigating to it, optionally with a custom filename.
notes: Only works for same-origin URLs (or ones with appropriate CORS headers).
